one_liner: Fixed-buffer JS-to-WASM call protocol (TypeScript host, Zig/Rust modules); 3.3-6.9x faster than wasm-bindgen on 100+ element typed-array calls.
what_it_does: zaw replaces wasm-bindgen's per-call glue for numeric work: at start-up the host reserves one input and one output channel inside WebAssembly linear memory, and each call writes arguments into the input channel, runs an exported function that returns 0 (OK) or 1 (error), then reads results from the output channel. The TypeScript host (npm zaw 0.0.5) exposes instance.bind(export, writeFn, readFn) to build a typed JS function; the Zig and Rust sides (crate zaw 0.0.3, Zig package zig-v0.0.1) provide matching Reader/Writer APIs plus logging, error strings and panic messages. It is not a drop-in for wasm-bindgen: you hand-write both sides of each binding, and only u8, u32, i32, f32 and f64 scalars and arrays cross the boundary.
how_it_is_fast: There is no per-call allocation on either side: input arrays are copied with one TypedArray.set into a preallocated, 8-byte-aligned channel; the module reads them as slices in place and writes results into a slice of the output channel; the host returns a subarray view of that channel instead of copying the result out. wasm-bindgen, by contrast, mallocs the input in WASM, and returning a Vec allocates on the WASM side and copies into a new JS typed array. Bindings are generated once per arity with new Function and cached views are rebuilt only when memory.buffer changes after memory.grow. The example kernels use simd128 (Zig auto-vectorises, Rust shares one kernel crate with the wasm-bindgen build).
when_to_use: Offloading individual numeric kernels from a TypeScript/JavaScript app to Zig or Rust WASM when calls pass or return typed arrays of about 100 elements or more
Hot paths that return arrays from WASM: the repo's Transfer Out Float64Array bench is 4.3x to 10.7x faster than wasm-bindgen from 10 to 100,000 elements
Batched small operations (for example many 4x4 matrix multiplies per call) where wasm-bindgen's per-call Vec allocation dominates: 1.7x to 4.0x faster than wasm-bindgen at batch 10 to 1000
Teams that want error messages, panic text and logging from WASM without adopting wasm-bindgen or the Component Model
when_not_to_use: Tiny inputs: at 10 elements plain JavaScript was 1.66x faster than zaw's Rust build and 1.67x faster than its Zig build in the repo's own XOR bench
Input-heavy calls with a scalar result: in Transfer In Float64Array wasm-bindgen was 1.03x to 1.22x faster than zaw up to 10,000 elements
Strings, structs, closures, DOM or JS object interop: only numeric scalars, numeric arrays and UTF-8 byte strings are supported, so wasm-bindgen or web-sys is still the tool there
Results larger than the fixed channel sizes chosen at instantiation (the benchmarks use 1,000,000 bytes each way); the module traps or panics on overflow rather than growing
Code that needs a stable API: npm 0.0.5, crate 0.0.3, Zig package 0.0.1, Go host 'coming later', single company maintainer

integration.form: module (npm zaw for the host) plus crate (Rust) or Zig package for the WASM side
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; the build examples use wasm-opt (Binaryen) and wasm2wat, and the wasm-bindgen baseline needs wasm-pack
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.16.0 on main (benchmarks predate that upgrade); Rust stable with target wasm32-unknown-unknown and -C link-arg=--import-memory; a JS runtime with WebAssembly SIMD for the simd128 example builds; a host that allows new Function
integration.platforms: any WebAssembly host where the TypeScript host can create a WebAssembly.Memory and pass it as env.memory (Node, browsers); the module must import its memory
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Each instance owns a single input and a single output channel, so calls are serialised and a returned array is only valid until the next call on that instance; use one instance per worker.

gotchas: Harness asymmetries behind the headline ratios: the JS XOR baseline allocates a fresh zero-filled Int32Array on every call and the JS 4x4 matmul baseline makes two slice() copies plus a new Float32Array per matrix and discards the results, while zaw returns a reused subarray view; the JS loop works out to about 6.1 ns per element at 100 elements and 1.3 ns at 100,000 versus zaw Rust's 0.095 ns (derived from page data), so the up-to-14x and 20-24x figures mostly measure JS allocation, not compute. All numbers are one Node run via vitest bench (Node version not stated, no browser runs).

Returned arrays are views into the output channel: the next call on the same instance overwrites them and a later memory.grow detaches them, so copy (slice) anything you keep, which gives back part of the advantage over wasm-bindgen.
The TypeScript host builds bindings with new Function, which fails where string code generation is blocked (a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-eval', and runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers).

Low-level defects in the module-side channel code: the Rust Channel holds five overlapping &mut slices of one buffer created with unsafe from_raw_parts_mut (aliasing undefined behaviour under Rust's rules, though it works with current compilers), and Zig's checkOffset tests offset >= capacity, so a payload that exactly fills a channel panics with 'Channel out of bounds' (the Rust side uses >).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick zaw over the catalogued wasm-bindgen entry when the hot path is a numeric kernel called often with typed arrays of 100+ elements, especially when it returns arrays; keep wasm-bindgen (and web-sys) for DOM work, strings and rich types. The other siblings (hash-wasm, DuckDB-Wasm, Loro, tfjs-backend-wasm and the like) are finished WASM libraries, not interop layers; zaw is a way to build such a library's call boundary.
verified_claims_summary: docs/benchmarks.md is one first-party vitest bench run in Node on an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D (Node, Zig and Rust versions not stated, run before the 2026-05-24 Zig 0.16 upgrade): XOR of a scalar into an Int32Array, zaw's Rust build vs a plain JS loop 6.0x at 100 elements up to 13.75x at 100,000 and vs wasm-bindgen 3.3x to 6.9x; JS wins at 10 elements; zaw's Zig build reaches 6-10x vs JS. Release builds used wasm-opt -O4 with simd128 for zaw, and wasm-pack's defaults with simd128 for the wasm-bindgen baseline.
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-05-24, two closed issues, one open PR) and Apache-2.0, but pre-1.0 (npm 0.0.5, crate 0.0.3) from one company; the protocol is small enough to vendor or reimplement, and the benchmark should be re-run in your target browser before trusting the ratios.
